4a503eb43281bb336df52e8e595f944b1ed5ca74.title: Supplied-propensity minimax rate
4a503eb43281bb336df52e8e595f944b1ed5ca74.body:
Fix public parameters satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Nuisance smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\le1\) and \(0<\beta\le1\).
\item \textbf{(Effect smoothness.)} \(1\le\gamma\le3\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge10\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) be the primitive class in \(\cref{obj:def:primitive-class}\), and let \(R^e(n,m)\) be the supplied-propensity minimax risk in \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-risk}\). Define the evaluation profile and supplied-propensity rate by
\[
x_0=(1/2,\ldots,1/2),
\qquad
r_o(n)=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
There exist real constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), depending on the fixed public parameters, such that, for every pair of integers \(n\ge2\) and \(m\ge0\),
\[
c\,r_o(n)\le R^e(n,m)\le C\,r_o(n).
\]

The upper bound is attained by the clipped known-design degree-two local polynomial decision
\[
\begin{aligned}
h&=n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},\\
T^e(\mathcal D_{n,m},U,e)
&=
\mathrm{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}
\left[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}
w_h(X_i)\,r_0^\top r(X_i)
\left\{
\frac{A_iY_i}{e(X_i)}
-
\frac{(1-A_i)Y_i}{1-e(X_i)}
\right\}
\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) is the original dataset, \(U\) is its independent uniform randomizer, \(w_h\) is the localization density under the known uniform design, \(r\) is the scaled orthonormal degree-two polynomial basis vector, and \(r_0=r(x_0)\). For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the decision supplied with the designated admissible propensity \(e_P\) is measurable and satisfies
\[
\left|T^e(\mathcal D_{n,m},U,e_P)\right|\le\frac34
\quad\text{for every }(\mathcal D_{n,m},U),
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}
\left[
\left|
T^e(\mathcal D_{n,m},U,e_P)-\tau_P(x_0)
\right|
\right]
\le C\,r_o(n).
\]
The sampling law \(\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)\) consists of \(n\) independent labeled records, \(m\) independent outcome-free covariate-treatment records, and the independent uniform randomizer; \(\tau_P\) is the canonical contrast from \(\cref{obj:def:primitive-class}\).

The same lower bound holds for the minimax risk restricted to the same-class subfamily with \(e_P=\mu_{0,P}=1/2\):
\[
c\,r_o(n)
\le
\inf_{T^e}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal M\\ e_P=\mu_{0,P}=1/2}}
\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}
\left[
\left|
T^e(\mathcal D_{n,m},U,e_P)-\tau_P(x_0)
\right|
\right],
\]
where the infimum uses the supplied-propensity decision class of \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-risk}\).

1b646d4dcc3ab5481d9609e728e7f6ed651e6ece.title: Sharp annotation and acquisition thresholds
1b646d4dcc3ab5481d9609e728e7f6ed651e6ece.body:
Fix public parameters satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Nuisance smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\le1\) and \(0<\beta\le1\).
\item \textbf{(Effect smoothness.)} \(1\le\gamma\le3\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge10\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(R(n,m)\) be the minimax absolute-error risk in
\cref{obj:def:minimax}, and let \(R^e(n,m)\) be the supplied-propensity
minimax risk in \cref{obj:def:oracle-risk}, for the primitive class
\(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) in
\cref{obj:def:primitive-class}. Define the total treatment-record count
\(N\), the summed nuisance smoothness \(S\), the rate denominator
\(\Delta\), the smoothness threshold \(S_{\mathrm{crit}}\), the
total-record growth exponent \(q_*\), and the oracle rate \(r_o\) by
\[
N=n+m,\qquad S=\alpha+\beta,\qquad
\Delta=2\gamma+d+\frac{\gamma d}{S},\qquad
S_{\mathrm{crit}}=\frac{\gamma d}{2\gamma+d},\qquad
q_*=\frac{\gamma d}{S(2\gamma+d)},\qquad
r_o(n)=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
Write \(r_*(n,m)\) for the sharp rate
\(r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) of \cref{obj:def:sharp-rate},
whose explicit formula is
\[
r_*(n,m)=
\max\left\{r_o(n),\,[n(n+m)]^{-\gamma/\Delta}\right\}.
\]

For every auxiliary-size sequence \((m_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) with
\(m_n\in\mathbb N\), the following statements are equivalent, with all
asymptotic statements taken as \(n\to\infty\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \(\displaystyle \frac{R(n,m_n)}{R^e(n,m_n)}=O(1)\).
\item \(r_*(n,m_n)=O(r_o(n))\).
\item There exists a finite real tolerance \(\zeta\ge1\) such that
\((n,m_n)\in\mathcal B_*(\zeta)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\),
where \(\mathcal B_*(\zeta)\) is defined in
\cref{obj:def:annotation-region}.
\item \(\displaystyle
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{n+m_n}{n^{q_*}}>0\),
where the lower limit is taken in the extended nonnegative reals.
\end{itemize}
For every such sequence, strict asymptotic improvement is characterized by
\[
\frac{R(n,m_n)}{R(n,0)}\longrightarrow0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{r_*(n,m_n)}{r_*(n,0)}\longrightarrow0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
S<S_{\mathrm{crit}}\ \text{and}\ \frac{m_n}{n}\longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
Moreover, \(S<S_{\mathrm{crit}}\) implies \(q_*>1\). For every sequence
with \(m_n/n=O(1)\), both comparisons hold:
\[
R(n,m_n)=O(R(n,0)),
\qquad
R(n,0)=O(R(n,m_n)).
\]
If \(S\ge S_{\mathrm{crit}}\), then
\(R(n,m_n)/R^e(n,m_n)=O(1)\) for every auxiliary-size sequence.

There exist real constants \(c,C\), depending on the fixed public
parameters, with \(0<c\le C\), such that, for every
\(n,m\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge2\),
\[
c\,r_*(n,m)\le R(n,m)\le C\,r_*(n,m).
\]
For all these sample sizes, the sharp rate has the exact branches
\[
r_*(n,m)=
\begin{cases}
r_o(n),& S\ge S_{\mathrm{crit}},\\
(nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta},
  & S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\quad N\le n^{q_*},\\
r_o(n),
  & S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\quad N\ge n^{q_*}.
\end{cases}
\]
Whenever \(N=n^{q_*}\), the two formulas agree:
\[
(nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta}=r_o(n).
\]
In particular, for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
r_*(n,0)=
\begin{cases}
n^{-2\gamma/\Delta},&S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\\
r_o(n),&S\ge S_{\mathrm{crit}}.
\end{cases}
\]
The numerical benchmark with average nuisance smoothness
\(s_{\mathrm{pub}}=S/2\) equals \(r_*(n,0)\) for every
\(n\in\mathbb N\). Explicitly, for \(n\ge1\),
\[
r_*(n,0)=
\begin{cases}
n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s_{\mathrm{pub}}))},
& s_{\mathrm{pub}}<\dfrac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)},\\
n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},
& s_{\mathrm{pub}}\ge\dfrac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)}.
\end{cases}
\]
At \(n=0\), both the numerical benchmark and \(r_*(n,0)\) equal zero.

Finally, there exist real constants \(c>0\) and \(C>0\), possibly
different from those above and depending on the fixed public parameters,
such that the following acquisition guarantees hold for every target
absolute-error scale \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and every
\(n,m\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge2\).

If there exists a Borel decision \(T\) in the original experiment such
that
\[
\mathcal R_{n,m}(T,P)\le\varepsilon
\qquad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal M,
\]
where the risk is defined in \cref{obj:def:risk}, then
\[
c\,\varepsilon^{-(2+d/\gamma)}\le n,
\qquad
c\,\varepsilon^{-(2+d/\gamma+d/S)}\le n(n+m).
\]
Conversely, if
\[
C\,\varepsilon^{-(2+d/\gamma)}\le n,
\qquad
C\,\varepsilon^{-(2+d/\gamma+d/S)}\le n(n+m),
\]
then the sharp decision \(T_*\) of \cref{obj:def:sharp-decision} is
Borel measurable and satisfies
\[
\mathcal R_{n,m}(T_*,P)\le\varepsilon
\qquad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal M.
\]
At the rate level, the acquisition conditions are exact:
\[
r_*(n,m)\le\varepsilon
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\varepsilon^{-(2+d/\gamma)}\le n
\ \text{and}\
\varepsilon^{-(2+d/\gamma+d/S)}\le n(n+m).
\]
The total count also satisfies \(n\le n+m\).

d4d5638d3048e037f34246b3630b108816d1f3eb.title: Population quadratic form positivity
d4d5638d3048e037f34246b3630b108816d1f3eb.body:
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Public parameters.)} The dimension \(d\) is a positive integer, \(0<\alpha\le1\), \(0<\beta\le1\), \(1\le\gamma\le3\), and \(L\ge10\).
\item \textbf{(Primitive law.)} \(P\in\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), with designated propensity witness \(e_P\), as in \cref{obj:def:primitive-class}.
\item \textbf{(Sample sizes.)} \(n,m\) are nonnegative integers with \(n\ge2\).
\item \textbf{(Localization and projection.)} \(0<h\le1/2\) and \(J\ge1\) is an integer, with projection \(\Pi_J\) as in \cref{obj:def:projection}.
\end{itemize}
Let \(\nu_h\) be the localization measure, \(Q_{P,h,J}\) the population expectation of the symmetrized empirical matrix, and \(p_v\) the coarse polynomial with coefficient vector \(v\), defined by
\[
d\nu_h(x)=h^{-d}\mathbf 1_{C_h}(x)\,dx,\qquad
Q_{P,h,J}=\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}
  [\widehat Q_{h,J}],\qquad
p_v(x)=\sum_{u=1}^{q}r_u(x)v_u.
\]
Here the coarse basis is indexed by the multi-indices of total degree at most two. For every \(v\in\mathbb R^q\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
v^\top Q_{P,h,J}v
&=\int e_P(x)\bigl(1-e_P(x)\bigr)p_v(x)^2\,d\nu_h(x)\\
&\quad+\int
\bigl(e_P(x)p_v(x)-\Pi_J(e_Pp_v)(x)\bigr)^2\,d\nu_h(x)\\
&\ge \frac{3}{16}\sum_{u=1}^{q}v_u^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

ad29c5aeb911c01c4de26834497f45f7edd03d19.title: Sharp annotation frontier
ad29c5aeb911c01c4de26834497f45f7edd03d19.body:
Fix public parameters \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\in\mathbb R\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Nuisance smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\le1\) and \(0<\beta\le1\).
\item \textbf{(Effect smoothness.)} \(1\le\gamma\le3\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge10\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) be the sharp rate in \(\cref{obj:def:sharp-rate}\), let \(T_*\) be the total data-only decision in \(\cref{obj:def:sharp-decision}\), and let \(R(n,m)\) be the minimax risk over the primitive class \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax}\).

There exist real constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), depending on the fixed public parameters, such that simultaneously for every \(n,m\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge2\), \(T_*\) is Borel measurable and
\[
c\,r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
\le R(n,m)
\le \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R_{n,m}(T_*,P)
\le C\,r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L).
\]
Moreover, every Borel real-valued decision \(T\) based on the original dataset and the independent uniform randomizer satisfies
\[
c\,r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
\le \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R_{n,m}(T,P).
\]

For these same sample sizes, define the total treatment-record count \(N\), the sum of nuisance smoothness orders \(S\), the rate denominator \(\Delta\), the smoothness threshold \(S_{\mathrm{crit}}\), the total-record exponent \(q_*\), and the supplied-propensity order \(r_o(n)\) by
\[
N=n+m,\qquad S=\alpha+\beta,\qquad
\Delta=2\gamma+d+\frac{\gamma d}{\alpha+\beta},
\]
\[
S_{\mathrm{crit}}=\frac{\gamma d}{2\gamma+d},
\qquad
q_*=\frac{\gamma d}{(\alpha+\beta)(2\gamma+d)},
\qquad
r_o(n)=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
Writing \(r_*\) for the sharp rate with its arguments suppressed, its branches are
\[
r_*=
\begin{cases}
r_o(n), & S\ge S_{\mathrm{crit}},\\
(nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta}, & S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\quad N\le n^{q_*},\\
r_o(n), & S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\quad N\ge n^{q_*}.
\end{cases}
\]
At the boundary \(N=n^{q_*}\), the two rate formulas coincide:
\[
(nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta}=r_o(n).
\]

a222f7cc27e8b82d1c6d4367b068853c2f4680fd.title: Local polynomial projection bounds
a222f7cc27e8b82d1c6d4367b068853c2f4680fd.body:
Fix public parameters \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\in\mathbb R\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\le1\), \(0<\beta\le1\), and \(1\le\gamma\le3\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge10\).
\end{itemize}
There exists a finite constant \(C=C(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)>0\) such that, for every primitive law \(P\in\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:primitive-class}\), every \(h\in\mathbb R\) with \(0<h\le1/2\), and every integer \(J\ge1\), the following statements hold for the bases and projection of \(\cref{obj:def:projection}\).

Let \(p\) be the Taylor polynomial of the canonical contrast \(\tau_P\) at the center \(x_0=(1/2,\ldots,1/2)\), of degree
\[
p_*=\lceil\gamma\rceil-1.
\]
There exists a coarse coefficient vector \(\vartheta\) such that its represented polynomial \(p_\vartheta(x)=r(x)^\top\vartheta\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{x\in C_h}|\tau_P(x)-p_\vartheta(x)|\le Ch^\gamma,
\qquad
\|\vartheta\|_2\le C,
\qquad
p_\vartheta(x_0)=\tau_P(x_0),
\]
and
\[
p_\vartheta(x)=p(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in C_h.
\]

The coarse basis vector and fine projection kernel satisfy
\[
\sup_{x\in C_h}\|r(x)\|_2\le C,
\qquad
\sup_{x\in C_h}\int |K_J(x,x')|\,d\nu_h(x')\le C,
\]
and
\[
\iint K_J(x,x')^2\,d\nu_h(x)\,d\nu_h(x')
=qJ^d=k,
\]
where \(q\) is the number of coarse multi-indices of total degree at most two and \(k=qJ^d\) is the fine projection rank.

Finally, with fine-cell side length \(\delta=h/J\), every coarse basis coordinate \(r_u\) satisfies
\[
\|e_Pr_u-\Pi_J(e_Pr_u)\|_{L_2(\nu_h)}
\le C\delta^\alpha,
\]
and the designated control-mean witness satisfies
\[
\|\mu_{0,P}-\Pi_J\mu_{0,P}\|_{L_2(\nu_h)}
\le C\delta^\beta.
\]

bface3a01e1f0819e9ca93a11eda041db049dda7.title: Rectangular estimator upper bounds
bface3a01e1f0819e9ca93a11eda041db049dda7.body:
Fix public parameters \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(d\) is an integer with \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\le1\), \(0<\beta\le1\), and \(1\le\gamma\le3\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge10\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) be the primitive class in \(\cref{obj:def:primitive-class}\). There exists a constant \(0<C<\infty\), depending only on these public parameters, for which both following guarantees hold.

For every pair of integers \(n\ge2\) and \(m\ge0\), every \(h\in(0,1/2]\), and every integer \(J\ge1\), set
\[
N=n+m,\qquad S=\alpha+\beta,\qquad \delta=\frac{h}{J}.
\]
The decision \(\widehat T_{h,J}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:estimator}\), viewed as a function of the original dataset and randomizer, is finite and Borel measurable, and its absolute-error risk from \(\cref{obj:def:risk}\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R_{n,m}(\widehat T_{h,J},P)
\le
C\min\left\{
1,\,
h^\gamma+\delta^S+(nh^d)^{-1/2}
+(nNh^d\delta^d)^{-1/2}
\right\}.
\]
For every pair of integers \(n\ge2\) and \(m\ge0\), the publicly tuned decision \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:tuning}\) is likewise finite and Borel measurable and satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R_{n,m}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}},P)
\le C r_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m),
\]
where \(r_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m)\) is the upper rate specified in \(\cref{obj:def:tuning}\).

c8a928b8b19e07499861445786df4ad1def49cc3.title: Rectangular sampling bound
c8a928b8b19e07499861445786df4ad1def49cc3.body:
Fix \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Nuisance smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\le1\) and \(0<\beta\le1\).
\item \textbf{(Effect smoothness.)} \(1\le\gamma\le3\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge10\).
\end{itemize}
There exists a finite constant \(C=C(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)>0\) such that the following bound holds for every primitive law \(P\in\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:primitive-class}, and every \(n,m,J\in\mathbb N\) and \(h\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample sizes.)} \(n\ge2\) and \(m\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Localization.)} \(0<h\le1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Resolution.)} \(J\ge1\).
\end{itemize}
Expectations are taken under \(\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)\), the product sampling law of \(n\) independent labeled records, \(m\) independent covariate-treatment records, and an independent uniform randomizer on \([0,1]\). Write \(N\) for the total treatment-record count, \(q\) for the number of polynomial multi-indices of total degree at most two, and \(k\) for the fine projection rank:
\[
N=n+m,\qquad q=\binom{d+2}{2},\qquad k=qJ^d.
\]
For the empirical response vector \(\widehat R_{h,J}\) and symmetrized corrected empirical matrix \(\widehat Q_{h,J}\), define their population expectations by
\[
\bar R=\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}\widehat R_{h,J},
\qquad
Q_{P,h,J}=\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}\widehat Q_{h,J}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}
 \bigl\|\widehat R_{h,J}-\bar R\bigr\|_2^2
+
\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}
 \bigl\|\widehat Q_{h,J}-Q_{P,h,J}\bigr\|_F^2
\le
C\left\{\frac{1}{nh^d}+\frac{k}{nNh^{2d}}\right\}.
\]

ea04162206d264203e49bee46cb1aa16baf9cee3.title: Hellinger calculus for blocks
ea04162206d264203e49bee46cb1aa16baf9cee3.body:
For probability laws \(\mathbb B,\mathbb C\) on a common measurable space, use the normalization of \(\cref{obj:def:hellinger}\):
\[
\mathsf h^2(\mathbb B,\mathbb C)
=\int\left(\sqrt{\frac{d\mathbb B}{d\xi}}
           -\sqrt{\frac{d\mathbb C}{d\xi}}\right)^2\,d\xi,
\qquad \xi=\mathbb B+\mathbb C.
\]
The following statements hold on arbitrary measurable spaces.

For any finite family of pairs of probability laws \(\mathbb B_{u_*},\mathbb C_{u_*}\), each pair on its respective common measurable space,
\[
\mathsf h^2\left(\bigotimes_{u_*}\mathbb B_{u_*},
                \bigotimes_{u_*}\mathbb C_{u_*}\right)
\le \sum_{u_*}\mathsf h^2(\mathbb B_{u_*},\mathbb C_{u_*}).
\]

Let \(\nu\) be a probability law on the conditioning space, and let \(\mathbb B_z,\mathbb C_z\) be probability kernels into a common measurable space. Suppose there exists a common s-finite reference kernel such that both kernels are represented, at every \(z\), by nonnegative extended-real densities with respect to that reference kernel, with both densities jointly measurable in the conditioning and outcome coordinates. Then
\[
\mathsf h^2\bigl(\nu(dz)\mathbb B_z(dw),
                \nu(dz)\mathbb C_z(dw)\bigr)
=\int \mathsf h^2(\mathbb B_z,\mathbb C_z)\,d\nu(z).
\]

For any probability laws \(\mathbb B,\mathbb C\) on a common measurable space and any probability law \(\nu\) on another measurable space,
\[
\mathsf h^2(\mathbb B\otimes\nu,\mathbb C\otimes\nu)
=\mathsf h^2(\mathbb B,\mathbb C).
\]

3f6c995f0d6d403461757452a1da86902f74b49d.title: Nuisance frontier lower bound
3f6c995f0d6d403461757452a1da86902f74b49d.body:
Fix \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\in\mathbb R\). Define the nuisance smoothness sum \(S\), the smoothness threshold \(S_{\mathrm{crit}}\), the record-growth exponent \(q_*\), and the rate denominator \(\Delta\) by
\[
S=\alpha+\beta,\qquad
S_{\mathrm{crit}}=\frac{\gamma d}{2\gamma+d},\qquad
q_*=\frac{\gamma d}{(\alpha+\beta)(2\gamma+d)},\qquad
\Delta=2\gamma+d+\frac{\gamma d}{\alpha+\beta}.
\]
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Nuisance smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\le1\) and \(0<\beta\le1\).
\item \textbf{(Effect smoothness.)} \(1\le\gamma\le3\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge10\).
\item \textbf{(Frontier regime.)} \(S<S_{\mathrm{crit}}\).
\end{itemize}
There exists a constant \(c>0\), depending on the fixed public parameters, such that for every \(n,m\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge2\), the total treatment-record count \(N=n+m\) satisfying
\[
n\le N\le n^{q_*}
\]
obeys the following bound for the minimax risk \(R(n,m)\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax}:
\[
R(n,m)\ge c(nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta}.
\]

75deec56b09d10d369ef3dcef34a395a698e2918.title: Marked component certificate
75deec56b09d10d369ef3dcef34a395a698e2918.body:
Fix the dimension \(d\ge1\), smoothness parameters \(\alpha,\beta\in(0,1]\) and \(\gamma\in[1,3]\), and radius \(L\ge10\). Let \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) be the primitive class of \cref{obj:def:primitive-class}. There exist constants \(c\in(0,1]\), \(c_0>0\), and \(C>0\), depending only on these public parameters, such that the following holds for every pair of integers \(n,m\) and real parameters \(h,\delta,a,b\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample sizes.)} \(n\ge2\), \(m\ge0\), and the total record count is \(N=n+m\).
\item \textbf{(Scales.)} \(0<\delta\le h\le\tfrac12\).
\item \textbf{(Amplitudes.)} \(0<a\le c\delta^\alpha\) and \(0<b\le c\delta^\beta\).
\item \textbf{(Contrast calibration.)} \(ab\le ch^\gamma\).
\item \textbf{(Occupancy.)} \(N\delta^d\le c_0\).
\end{itemize}

For the prescribed construction \(\mathfrak C\) of \cref{obj:def:marked-handle}, the weights on the finite sign arrays satisfy, for each hypothesis \(\theta\in\{-1,+1\}\),
\[
w_\theta(\lambda,\eta)\ge0
\quad\text{for every }\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I},
\qquad
\sum_{\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I}}
w_\theta(\lambda,\eta)=1.
\]
Every constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal M\), and its canonical contrast agrees everywhere on the unit cube with the deterministic contrast of its hypothesis:
\[
P_{\theta,\lambda,\eta}\in\mathcal M,
\qquad
\tau_{P_{\theta,\lambda,\eta}}(x)=\tau_\theta(x)
\quad
\bigl(x\in[0,1]^d\bigr).
\]
Thus the finite priors \(\varpi_\theta\) of the construction are supported on \(\mathcal M\).

The designated propensity function \(e_P\), restricted to the unit cube, has the same distribution under \(\varpi_{+1}\) and \(\varpi_{-1}\). At the interior evaluation profile
\[
x_0=(1/2,\ldots,1/2),
\]
the contrasts satisfy
\[
\tau_\theta(x_0)=-2\theta ab,
\qquad
\tau_{-1}(x_0)-\tau_{+1}(x_0)=4ab,
\qquad
cab\le4ab.
\]

Let \(M_{+1}\) and \(M_{-1}\) be the fixed-size mixture laws of the original-record experiment, with \(n\) labeled records and \(m\) auxiliary covariate-treatment records, under the respective priors. With the unhalved squared Hellinger distance of \cref{obj:def:hellinger},
\[
H^2(M_{+1},M_{-1})
\le CnNh^d\delta^da^2b^2.
\]

For every integer \(k_{\mathrm{aux}}\ge0\), the auxiliary mixture laws agree:
\[
\int P_{XA}^{\otimes k_{\mathrm{aux}}}\,d\varpi_{+1}(P)
=
\int P_{XA}^{\otimes k_{\mathrm{aux}}}\,d\varpi_{-1}(P).
\]
Their explicit conditional mixture kernels also agree for every collection of \(k_{\mathrm{aux}}\) covariates in \([0,1]^d\). For each hypothesis and every covariate \(x\in[0,1]^d\), the singleton labeled mixture has conditional law uniform on \(\{0,1\}^2\) for the treatment and observed response.

Conditional on all \(N\) covariates, form the graph with vertices given by the records whose covariates lie in the localization cube \(C_h\) of \cref{obj:def:marked-handle}, and edges between distinct vertices whose maximum-norm covariate distance is at most \(2\delta\). The conditional mixed laws factor across the connected components of this graph. Every auxiliary-only component and every singleton labeled component has the same conditional law under both hypotheses.

970328c9b6f3bc0f88a0863e823d012709394758.title: Absolute-loss fuzzy testing bound
970328c9b6f3bc0f88a0863e823d012709394758.body:
Let \((\mathbb B_z)\) and \((\mathbb C_z)\) be probability kernels from a common measurable index space to a common measurable observation space, and let \(\omega\) be a probability prior on the index space. Let \(v_0\ge1\) be an integer, let \(\mathcal M\) be a model of measures containing \(\mathbb B_z\) and \(\mathbb C_z\) for every \(z\), and let \(\Psi\) be a real-valued functional on measures. Use the squared Hellinger distance of \cref{obj:def:hellinger}, with normalization
\[
\mathsf h^2(\mathbb B,\mathbb C)
=
\int
\left(
\sqrt{\frac{d\mathbb B}{d\xi}}
-
\sqrt{\frac{d\mathbb C}{d\xi}}
\right)^2\,d\xi,
\qquad
\xi=\mathbb B+\mathbb C.
\]
Suppose the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Constants.)} The separation bound \(s_0\) and distance bound \(u_0\) satisfy \(s_0>0\) and \(0\le u_0<2\).
\item \textbf{(Separation.)} For every pair of indices \(z,z'\),
\[
\Psi(\mathbb B_z)-\Psi(\mathbb C_{z'})\ge s_0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Mixture distance.)} The product-law mixtures satisfy
\[
\mathsf h^2\left(
\int \mathbb B_z^{\otimes v_0}\,d\omega(z),
\int \mathbb C_z^{\otimes v_0}\,d\omega(z)
\right)\le u_0.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then every measurable real-valued decision \(\widehat\Psi\) on the \(v_0\)-observation sample space satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\int
\left|\widehat\Psi(w)-\Psi(P)\right|
\,dP^{\otimes v_0}(w)
\ge
\frac{s_0}{4}
\left\{1-\sqrt{u_0(1-u_0/4)}\right\},
\]
where the nonnegative loss integral is interpreted in the extended sense. This is the absolute-loss specialization of \citep[Section 3, Lemma 1]{KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024}.

390b0859a5a916891deb0c1b078b83bc5ba77550.title: Published CATE benchmark identities
390b0859a5a916891deb0c1b078b83bc5ba77550.body:
Let the dimension \(d\in\mathbb N\) and smoothness orders \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb R\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(1\le d\).
\item \textbf{(First nuisance smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\).
\item \textbf{(Second nuisance smoothness.)} \(0<\beta\).
\item \textbf{(Effect smoothness.)} \(1\le\gamma\).
\end{itemize}
Put \(s_{\mathrm{pub}}=(\alpha+\beta)/2\), the average nuisance smoothness. The numerical exponents and smoothness cutoff displayed in \citet[Section 3, Theorem 1]{KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024} satisfy
\[
\frac{1}{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s_{\mathrm{pub}})}
=\frac{2\gamma}{2\gamma+d+\gamma d/(\alpha+\beta)},
\qquad
\frac{1}{2+d/\gamma}=\frac{\gamma}{2\gamma+d},
\]
and
\[
s_{\mathrm{pub}}<\frac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\alpha+\beta<\frac{\gamma d}{2\gamma+d}.
\]
For every \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge2\), the numerical piecewise benchmark satisfies
\[
\begin{cases}
n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s_{\mathrm{pub}}))},
& s_{\mathrm{pub}}<(d/4)/(1+d/(2\gamma)),\\
n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},
& s_{\mathrm{pub}}\ge(d/4)/(1+d/(2\gamma))
\end{cases}
=
\max\left\{
n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
n^{-2\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\gamma d/(\alpha+\beta))}
\right\}.
\]

526b6f6fa7a5317511d8ff72c218b7055cc9dc07.title: Conditional treatment exchangeability
526b6f6fa7a5317511d8ff72c218b7055cc9dc07.body:
The treatment indicator \(A\) and the potential responses \(Y(0),Y(1)\) satisfy
\[
A\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X,
\]
where \(X\) is the covariate vector.

1c30a805fabb4d5b6cde7d91d7cb240f615c6181.title: Uniform propensity overlap
1c30a805fabb4d5b6cde7d91d7cb240f615c6181.body:
The designated Borel propensity witness \(e_P\) satisfies
\[
e_P(x)\in[1/4,3/4]
\qquad\text{for every }x\in[0,1]^d.
\]

2b3279331a1ffceeed5db4c6920003a19a9fab3f.title: Propensity Hölder smoothness
2b3279331a1ffceeed5db4c6920003a19a9fab3f.body:
The designated Borel propensity witness \(e_P\) satisfies
\[
\|e_P\|_{H^\alpha}\le L.
\]

0771a8e3807ab08c08be8e25aa3abefce1dc93a1.title: Control-mean Hölder smoothness
0771a8e3807ab08c08be8e25aa3abefce1dc93a1.body:
The designated Borel control-mean witness \(\mu_{0,P}\) satisfies
\[
\|\mu_{0,P}\|_{H^\beta}\le L.
\]

8437ba268da80a7e25bc7ae74841222078020426.title: Causal contrast Hölder smoothness
8437ba268da80a7e25bc7ae74841222078020426.body:
The canonical continuous causal contrast \(\tau_P\) satisfies
\[
\|\tau_P\|_{H^\gamma}\le L.
\]

a0da25af7b8b8c4b700bce542d944d7bb7ce009c.title: Control response interior bounds
a0da25af7b8b8c4b700bce542d944d7bb7ce009c.body:
The designated Borel control-mean function \(\mu_{0,P}\) satisfies
\[
\mu_{0,P}(x)\in[1/8,7/8]
\qquad\text{for every }x\in[0,1]^d.
\]

5bca6642ae13cbdf649c58ddae95a43a4b959ce5.title: Treated response interior bounds
5bca6642ae13cbdf649c58ddae95a43a4b959ce5.body:
The designated Borel treated-mean function \(\mu_{1,P}\) satisfies
\[
\mu_{1,P}(x)\in[1/8,7/8]
\qquad\text{for every }x\in[0,1]^d.
\]

c181accaa9a2d400948d778352d133549f1adc48.title: Original experiment sampling law
c181accaa9a2d400948d778352d133549f1adc48.body:
The original dataset \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) and independent uniform randomizer \(U\) have joint law
\[
\mathcal L_P(\mathcal D_{n,m},U)=\mathsf E_{n,m}(P),
\]
where \(\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)\) is the product sampling law of the original dataset and randomizer.

2fff35362ad5a642b993b2fd525050e4e6994fbb.title: Hölder norm $\|f\|_{H^s}$

8c3a5d33311fd65c4292da7783a41d8e4b78e42e.title: Primitive law class $\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)$
8c3a5d33311fd65c4292da7783a41d8e4b78e42e.body:
The class \(\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) consists of primitive Borel laws \(P=\mathcal L(X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\), where \(X\) is the covariate vector on \([0,1]^d\), \(A\) is the binary treatment indicator, and \(Y(0),Y(1)\) are the binary potential responses under control and treatment, for which there exist Borel functions
\[
g_e,g_0,g_1:[0,1]^d\longrightarrow[0,1]
\]
satisfying
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_e(X)&=\mathbb E_P[A\mid X] &&P\text{-almost surely},\\
g_0(X)&=\mathbb E_P[Y(0)\mid X] &&P\text{-almost surely},\\
g_1(X)&=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)\mid X] &&P\text{-almost surely},
\end{aligned}
\]
and the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Uniform design.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:uniform-design},
\[
\mathcal L_P(X)=\mathrm{Unif}([0,1]^d).
\]
\item \textbf{(Exchangeability.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:exchangeability},
\[
A\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X.
\]
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:overlap},
\[
g_e(x)\in[1/4,3/4]
\qquad(\forall x\in[0,1]^d).
\]
\item \textbf{(Propensity smoothness.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:propensity-holder},
\[
\|g_e\|_{H^\alpha}\le L.
\]
\item \textbf{(Control smoothness.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:control-holder},
\[
\|g_0\|_{H^\beta}\le L.
\]
\item \textbf{(Propensity smoothness.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:effect-holder},
\[
\|g_1-g_0\|_{H^\gamma}\le L.
\]
\item \textbf{(Control interior bounds.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:control-interior},
\[
g_0(x)\in[1/8,7/8]
\qquad(\forall x\in[0,1]^d).
\]
\item \textbf{(Treated interior bounds.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:treated-interior},
\[
g_1(x)\in[1/8,7/8]
\qquad(\forall x\in[0,1]^d).
\]
\end{itemize}
For each admitted law, \(e_P,\mu_{0,P},\mu_{1,P}\) designate admissible functions \(g_e,g_0,g_1\), respectively. The canonical continuous conditional causal contrast \(\tau_P\) is the continuous representative of the almost-sure conditional causal contrast and satisfies
\[
\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x)
\qquad(\forall x\in[0,1]^d).
\]
At the fixed public parameters, write \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).

be53c5d9e11fe69cd27cdb6082c8f85dfbaf48a1.title: Absolute-error risk $\mathcal R_{n,m}(T,P)$
be53c5d9e11fe69cd27cdb6082c8f85dfbaf48a1.body:
The absolute-error risk is
\[
\mathcal R_{n,m}(T,P)
=
\int
\left|T(\mathcal D_{n,m},U)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|
\,d\mathsf E_{n,m}(P).
\]
Here \(T\) is a Borel real-valued decision using the original dataset \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) and independent uniform randomizer \(U\), \(x_0\) is the fixed interior covariate profile, and \(\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)\) is the product sampling law of the original dataset and randomizer. The target \(\tau_P(x_0)\) is the canonical conditional causal contrast from \cref{obj:def:primitive-class}.

7e0c9c101fe8307911a72623fa3feffeabe2fc15.title: Public tuning \(h_*,J_*,\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}\)
7e0c9c101fe8307911a72623fa3feffeabe2fc15.body:
The localization scale \(h_*\), grid resolution \(J_*\), and tuned decision \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}\) are
\[
h_*=\frac12\max\left\{n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},(nN)^{-1/\Delta}\right\},
\qquad
J_*=\left\lceil h_*^{-\max\{0,\gamma/S-1\}}\right\rceil,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}=\widehat T_{h_*,J_*},
\]
where \(N\) is the total treatment-record count, \(S\) is the sum of the propensity and control-mean Hölder orders, and \(\Delta\) is the denominator governing the unequal-channel rate exponent.

468810bd23fc8467f41bc3842f863096a7993c64.title: Squared Hellinger distance \(H^2\)
468810bd23fc8467f41bc3842f863096a7993c64.body:
The squared Hellinger distance between the positive- and negative-hypothesis mixture laws \(M_{+1}\) and \(M_{-1}\) is
\[
H^2(M_{+1},M_{-1})
=
\int
\left(
\sqrt{\frac{dM_{+1}}{d(M_{+1}+M_{-1})}}
-
\sqrt{\frac{dM_{-1}}{d(M_{+1}+M_{-1})}}
\right)^2
\,d(M_{+1}+M_{-1}).
\]

08b37b7240c1e376439a58e7ec53ad842928d346.title: Finite-prior construction \(\mathfrak C\)
08b37b7240c1e376439a58e7ec53ad842928d346.body:
The construction \(\mathfrak C\) takes inputs \((h,\delta,a,b)\) satisfying \(0<\delta\le h\le1/2\) and \(a,b>0\), at the public parameters \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and fixed interior covariate profile \(x_0\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the real functions
\[
\chi(u)=
\begin{cases}
\exp(-1/u),&u>0,\\
0,&u\le0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\vartheta(u)=\frac{\pi}{2}\frac{\chi(u)}{\chi(u)+\chi(1-u)},
\qquad u\in\mathbb R,
\]
and, for each \(z\in\mathbb Z\),
\[
\omega_z(u)=
\begin{cases}
\sin\vartheta(u-z+1),&z-1\le u\le z,\\
\cos\vartheta(u-z),&z\le u\le z+1,\\
0,&u\notin[z-1,z+1].
\end{cases}
\]
The two expressions at \(u=z\) agree.

\item For \(w\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(x\in[0,1]^d\), define the localization bump and fine-scale frame by
\[
B(w)=\prod_{v=1}^d\frac{\chi(1-4w_v^2)}{\chi(1)},
\qquad
B_h(x)=B\bigl((x-x_0)/h\bigr),
\]
\[
\psi_{\mathbf z}(x)=
\prod_{v=1}^d
\omega_{z_v}\bigl((x_v-x_{0,v})/\delta\bigr),
\]
\[
\mathcal I=
\left\{\mathbf z\in\mathbb Z^d:
|z_v|\le1+\frac{h}{2\delta}
\text{ for every }v\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\right\},
\qquad
\phi_{\mathbf z}(x)=B_h(x)\psi_{\mathbf z}(x),
\quad \mathbf z\in\mathcal I.
\]

\item For sign arrays \(\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I}\), define
\[
F_\lambda(x)=
\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}\lambda_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}(x),
\qquad
G_\eta(x)=
\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}\eta_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}(x).
\]
For each hypothesis index \(\theta\in\{-1,+1\}\), define the sign-pair correlation and product weights by
\[
\rho_\theta=\frac{\theta}{2},
\qquad
w_\theta(\lambda,\eta)=
\prod_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}
\frac{1+\rho_\theta\lambda_{\mathbf z}\eta_{\mathbf z}}{4}.
\]

\item Define the propensity, contrast, and potential-response means by
\[
e_\lambda(x)=\frac12+aF_\lambda(x),
\qquad
\tau_\theta(x)=-4ab\rho_\theta B_h(x)^2,
\]
\[
\mu_{0,\theta,\eta}(x)=
\frac12+bG_\eta(x)-\frac12\tau_\theta(x),
\qquad
\mu_{1,\theta,\eta}(x)=
\frac12+bG_\eta(x)+\frac12\tau_\theta(x).
\]
The probability-valued domain consists of inputs satisfying
\[
e_\lambda(x),\ \mu_{0,\theta,\eta}(x),\
\mu_{1,\theta,\eta}(x)\in[0,1]
\quad
\text{for every }\theta\in\{-1,+1\},\
\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I},\
x\in[0,1]^d.
\]
On this domain, define the primitive Borel law \(P_{\theta,\lambda,\eta}\) by
\[
X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d),
\qquad
\mathcal L\bigl(A,Y(0),Y(1)\mid X=x\bigr)
=
\operatorname{Bernoulli}\bigl(e_\lambda(x)\bigr)
\otimes
\operatorname{Bernoulli}\bigl(\mu_{0,\theta,\eta}(x)\bigr)
\otimes
\operatorname{Bernoulli}\bigl(\mu_{1,\theta,\eta}(x)\bigr).
\]
Here \(X\) is the covariate vector, \(A\) is the binary treatment indicator, and \(Y(0),Y(1)\) are the binary potential responses under control and treatment. The prescribed functions \(e_\lambda,\mu_{0,\theta,\eta},\mu_{1,\theta,\eta}\) are the designated conditional-margin functions of this law.

\item Output the contrasts and finite pushforward measures
\[
\mathfrak C(h,\delta,a,b)
=
\bigl((\tau_\theta,\varpi_\theta)\bigr)_{\theta\in\{-1,+1\}},
\qquad
\varpi_\theta=
\sum_{\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I}}
w_\theta(\lambda,\eta)\,
\operatorname{Dirac}(P_{\theta,\lambda,\eta}),
\]
where \(\operatorname{Dirac}(P)\) is the unit point mass at the primitive law \(P\).
\end{enumerate}

f5d026ae892d2821af99437d1ab9a0b3499db0d9.title: Sharp rate and decision \((r_*,T_*)\)
f5d026ae892d2821af99437d1ab9a0b3499db0d9.body:
The procedure takes the public parameters \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), sample sizes \((n,m)\), and fixed interior covariate profile \(x_0\), with localization scale \(h\) and grid resolution \(J\) as tuning parameters.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Starting from the local polynomial decision \(\widehat T_{h,J}\), use polynomial reproduction and unequal-channel projection correction to derive a risk bound for the conditional causal contrast \(\tau_P(x_0)\).

\item Optimize localization and resolution over the public parameters.

\item Match the data-only risk with fixed-size common-propensity mixtures from the finite-prior construction \(\mathfrak C\), treating sparse and dense treatment-record occupancy separately.

\item Output the sharp rate and attaining decision,
\[
(r_*,T_*).
\]
\end{enumerate}

7e760d9eeb0ffcd0da9afe17413bdb80ce28fe89.title: Annotation region \(\mathcal B_*(\zeta)\)
7e760d9eeb0ffcd0da9afe17413bdb80ce28fe89.body:
The annotation region at tolerance \(\zeta\) is
\[
\mathcal B_*(\zeta)=
\left\{
(n,m)\in\mathbb N_{\ge2}\times\mathbb N_0:
r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\le\zeta r_o(n)
\right\},
\]
where \(r_*\) is the sharp rate and \(r_o(n)\) is the supplied-propensity point-estimation order.

aa798c57e9ae5938b998f84a3cbead2b805050af.title: Sharp rate \(r_*\)
aa798c57e9ae5938b998f84a3cbead2b805050af.body:
The sharp rate at the public class parameters is
\[
r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
=
\max\left\{
n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
[n(n+m)]^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\gamma d/(\alpha+\beta))}
\right\}
=
r_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m),
\]
where \(r_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m)\) is the maximum of the supplied-propensity and unequal-channel rate orders.

9b35fcb26c39d8b72d0a4204f8aba50f00683cb1.title: Minimax risk \(R(n,m)\)
9b35fcb26c39d8b72d0a4204f8aba50f00683cb1.body:
\[
R(n,m)=\inf_{T\ {\rm Borel}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R_{n,m}(T,P).
\]
Here \(\mathcal M\) is the primitive law class at the fixed public parameters, and \(\mathcal R_{n,m}(T,P)\) is the expected absolute error for the point contrast under law \(P\). The infimum ranges over Borel real-valued decisions \(T\) using the original dataset of \(n\) labeled records and \(m\) independent outcome-free treatment records, together with an independent uniform randomizer.

1d0a6a9ac95043586f39a43e46540906a93bd2f0.title: Supplied-propensity risk \(R^e(n,m)\)
1d0a6a9ac95043586f39a43e46540906a93bd2f0.body:
\[
R^e(n,m)=\inf_{T^e}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\int
\left|T^e(\mathcal D_{n,m},U,e_P)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|
\,d\mathsf E_{n,m}(P).
\]
The infimum ranges over Borel real-valued decisions \(T^e\) receiving the original dataset \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), the independent uniform randomizer \(U\), and the designated admissible propensity function \(e_P\). Here \(\mathcal M\) is the primitive law class at the fixed public parameters, \(\tau_P\) is the canonical continuous conditional causal contrast, \(x_0\) is the fixed interior covariate profile, and \(\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)\) is the product sampling law of the dataset and randomizer.

d21d6d462728d072441b3364105ab678021c21b9.title: Projection \(\Pi_J\) and kernel \(K_J\)
d21d6d462728d072441b3364105ab678021c21b9.body:
\[
\delta=\frac hJ,\qquad
K_J(x,x')=b(x)^\top b(x'),\qquad
\Pi_Jf(x)=\int K_J(x,x')f(x')\,d\nu_h(x').
\]
Here \(\delta\) is the fine-cell side length, \(h\) is the localization scale, \(J\) is the grid resolution, \(b\) is the cellwise orthonormal fine polynomial basis vector, and \(\nu_h\) is the uniform probability measure on the localization cube \(C_h\). Weighted basis expressions are zero outside \(C_h\).

935e69c0f7608518402f2d6f0a6b6c6115295094.title: Record roles \(\mathcal D^T,I_L,I_T\)
935e69c0f7608518402f2d6f0a6b6c6115295094.body:
Given the original dataset \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) of \(n\) labeled records and \(m\) independent outcome-free treatment records, form the two roles as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Concatenate the covariate-treatment pairs, with total treatment-record count \(N\):
\[
N=n+m,\qquad
\mathcal D^T=((X_i^T,A_i^T))_{i=1}^N,
\qquad
(X_i^T,A_i^T)=
\begin{cases}
(X_i,A_i),&1\le i\le n,\\
(\widetilde X_{i-n},\widetilde A_{i-n}),&n<i\le N.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(X\) denotes the covariate vector and \(A\) the binary treatment indicator; tildes denote auxiliary records.
\item Define the outcome-role count \(\ell\), treatment-role count \(t\), and their index sets:
\[
\ell=\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\qquad
t=N-\ell,\qquad
I_L=\{1,\ldots,\ell\},\qquad
I_T=\{\ell+1,\ldots,N\}.
\]
\item Output the outcome-role labeled records and treatment-role covariate-treatment pairs:
\[
\bigl((X_j,A_j,Y_j)\bigr)_{j\in I_L},
\qquad
\bigl((X_i^T,A_i^T)\bigr)_{i\in I_T}.
\]
Here \(Y_j\) is the observed response. Outcomes from treatment-role records are discarded.
\end{enumerate}

f832bcdbf9215059301d9b0c488abed62a33e5d1.title: Empirical moments \(\widehat R_{h,J},\widehat Q_{h,J}\)
f832bcdbf9215059301d9b0c488abed62a33e5d1.body:
Given the original dataset \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), localization scale \(h\), grid resolution \(J\), localization cube \(C_h\), localization density \(w_h\), coarse polynomial basis vector \(r\), and fine projection kernel \(K_J\), compute the moments as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Form the independent outcome and treatment roles, with counts and index sets
\[
N=n+m,\qquad
\ell=\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\qquad
t=N-\ell,\qquad
I_L=\{1,\ldots,\ell\},\qquad
I_T=\{\ell+1,\ldots,N\}.
\]
The treatment sequence consists of the covariate-treatment pairs
\[
(X_i^T,A_i^T)=
\begin{cases}
(X_i,A_i),&1\le i\le n,\\
(\widetilde X_{i-n},\widetilde A_{i-n}),&n<i\le N.
\end{cases}
\]
Use labeled records \((X_j,A_j,Y_j)\) for \(j\in I_L\) in the outcome role and pairs \((X_i^T,A_i^T)\) for \(i\in I_T\) in the treatment role. Treatment-role outcomes are discarded. Weighted basis expressions are zero outside \(C_h\).
\item Define the outcome-role empirical projection:
\[
\widehat\eta_J^L(x)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac1\ell\sum_{j\in I_L}
w_h(X_j)K_J(x,X_j)Y_j,&x\in C_h,\\
0,&x\notin C_h.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Define the empirical response vector:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat R_{h,J}
&=\frac1\ell\sum_{j\in I_L}w_h(X_j)r(X_j)A_jY_j
-\frac1t\sum_{i\in I_T}w_h(X_i^T)r(X_i^T)A_i^T
\widehat\eta_J^L(X_i^T)\\
&=\frac1\ell\sum_{j\in I_L}w_h(X_j)r(X_j)A_jY_j
-\frac1{t\ell}\sum_{i\in I_T}\sum_{j\in I_L}
w_h(X_i^T)w_h(X_j)r(X_i^T)A_i^T
K_J(X_i^T,X_j)Y_j.
\end{aligned}
\]
The response factor in the rectangular correction is \(Y_j\), and the first summand uses \(A_jY_j\). The nested and rectangular expressions define the same vector.
\item Define the unsymmetrized empirical matrix:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat Q^{\mathrm{raw}}_{h,J}
&=\frac1\ell\sum_{j\in I_L}w_h(X_j)r(X_j)r(X_j)^\top A_j\\
&\quad-\frac1{t\ell}\sum_{i\in I_T}\sum_{j\in I_L}
w_h(X_i^T)w_h(X_j)r(X_i^T)r(X_j)^\top
A_i^TA_jK_J(X_i^T,X_j).
\end{aligned}
\]
\item Output the response vector and symmetrized matrix:
\[
\left(\widehat R_{h,J},\widehat Q_{h,J}\right),
\qquad
\widehat Q_{h,J}
=\frac{\widehat Q^{\mathrm{raw}}_{h,J}
+(\widehat Q^{\mathrm{raw}}_{h,J})^\top}{2}.
\]
All inputs are observed in \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), including when \(m=0\).
\end{enumerate}

T_*(\mathcal D_{n,m},U)

For every original dataset \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) and independent uniform randomizer \(U\), this decision uses the prescribed empirical moments, empirical eigenvalue cutoff, clipping, role split, and public tuning parameters \(h_*\) and \(J_*\). Its value is independent of \(U\).

dba55035d1f23e5b85139a356eeb5e76c97e790d.title: Scaled coarse polynomial basis
dba55035d1f23e5b85139a356eeb5e76c97e790d.body:
The coarse polynomial basis vector \(r\), for dimension \(d\in\mathbb N\) and scale \(h\in\mathbb R\), is defined at each \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) by
\[
r(x)=
\left(
\prod_{i=1}^{d}
\begin{cases}
1, & \kappa_i=0,\\
\sqrt{12}\,\dfrac{x_i-\tfrac12}{h}, & \kappa_i=1,\\
\sqrt{5}\left(6\left(\dfrac{x_i-\tfrac12}{h}\right)^2-\tfrac12\right),
& \kappa_i=2
\end{cases}
\right)_{\kappa\in\mathbb N_0^d:\,\sum_{i=1}^{d}\kappa_i\le 2}.
\]
Division by zero is interpreted as zero, so this definition also specifies \(r\) at \(h=0\).

48d4b8010dd809a80a12879014b5e7b941806ed9.title: Response amplitude and means
48d4b8010dd809a80a12879014b5e7b941806ed9.body:
The response-mean perturbation amplitude \(b\in\mathbb R\) enters the constructed real-valued arm-mean functions as follows. For dimension \(d\in\mathbb N\), parameters \(h,\delta,a\in\mathbb R\), hypothesis sign \(\theta\in\{-1,+1\}\), and response signs \(\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I}\), indexed by the finite frame index set \(\mathcal I\) at scales \(h,\delta\), define, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_{0,\theta,\eta}(x)
&=\frac12+b\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}
  \eta_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}(x)
  +\theta ab\,B_h(x)^2,\\
\mu_{1,\theta,\eta}(x)
&=\frac12+b\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}
  \eta_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}(x)
  -\theta ab\,B_h(x)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\phi_{\mathbf z}(x)\) is the localized fine-scale frame entry and \(B_h(x)\) is the localization bump. The hypothesis sign and each response sign encode the corresponding Boolean value by assigning \(+1\) to true and \(-1\) to false; control and treatment correspond to false and true arm values, respectively.

c8916ef108842d02a2504f1cb782b1f3c7a9de2f.title: Rectangular risk upper bounds
c8916ef108842d02a2504f1cb782b1f3c7a9de2f.body:
Fix public parameters \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(d\) is an integer with \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} \(0<\alpha\le1\), \(0<\beta\le1\), and \(1\le\gamma\le3\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge10\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) be the primitive class in \cref{obj:def:primitive-class}. There exists a constant \(0<C<\infty\), depending only on these public parameters, for which both following guarantees hold.

For every pair of integers \(n\ge2\) and \(m\ge0\), every \(h\in(0,1/2]\), and every integer \(J\ge1\), set
\[
N=n+m,\qquad S=\alpha+\beta,\qquad \delta=\frac{h}{J}.
\]
The decision \(\widehat T_{h,J}\) of \cref{obj:def:estimator}, viewed as a function of the original dataset and randomizer, is finite and Borel measurable, and its absolute-error risk from \cref{obj:def:risk} satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R_{n,m}(\widehat T_{h,J},P)
\le
C\min\left\{
1,\,
h^\gamma+\delta^S+(nh^d)^{-1/2}
+(nNh^d\delta^d)^{-1/2}
\right\}.
\]
For every pair of integers \(n\ge2\) and \(m\ge0\), the publicly tuned decision \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}\) of \cref{obj:def:tuning} is likewise finite and Borel measurable and satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R_{n,m}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}},P)
\le C r_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m),
\]
where \(r_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m)\) is the upper rate specified in \cref{obj:def:sharp-rate}.

6e16577d38f36f2c71284c9609eddc3644169236.title: Observed response selection
6e16577d38f36f2c71284c9609eddc3644169236.body:
The observed response \(Y\) for a full record \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\), where \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) is the covariate vector for a nonnegative integer \(d\), \(A\in\{0,1\}\) is the treatment indicator, and \(Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\}\) are the potential responses under control and treatment, is defined by
\[
Y=
\begin{cases}
Y(0), & A=0,\\
Y(1), & A=1.
\end{cases}
\]
The corresponding observed record is \((X,A,Y)\).

714463645c120d6f09b3c577e548f53a0920622b.title: Sharp rate and decision pair
714463645c120d6f09b3c577e548f53a0920622b.body:
The frontier handle is the ordered pair \((r_*,T_*)\) for parameters \(d,n,m\in\mathbb N\) and \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb R\), where the sharp rate \(r_*\) and decision \(T_*\) are given by \cref{obj:def:sharp-rate,obj:def:sharp-decision}:
\[
r_*=
\max\left\{
n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
\bigl(n(n+m)\bigr)^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\gamma d/(\alpha+\beta))}
\right\},
\qquad
T_*(\mathcal D_{n,m},U)
=
\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}(\mathcal D_{n,m}).
\]
Here \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) is the original dataset, \(U\) is the randomizer coordinate, and \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}\) is the publicly tuned estimator of \cref{obj:def:tuning}.

5f2a06eedb69b81e89c9d2fa27ff299ecf263c07.title: Marked component construction certificate
5f2a06eedb69b81e89c9d2fa27ff299ecf263c07.body:
Fix the dimension \(d\ge1\), smoothness parameters \(\alpha,\beta\in(0,1]\) and \(\gamma\in[1,3]\), and radius \(L\ge10\). Let \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) be the primitive class of \cref{obj:def:primitive-class}. There exist constants \(c\in(0,1]\), \(c_0>0\), and \(C>0\), depending only on these public parameters, such that the following holds for every pair of integers \(n,m\) and real parameters \(h,\delta,a,b\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample sizes.)} \(n\ge2\), \(m\ge0\), and the total record count is \(N=n+m\).
\item \textbf{(Scales.)} \(0<\delta\le h\le\tfrac12\).
\item \textbf{(Amplitudes.)} \(0<a\le c\delta^\alpha\) and \(0<b\le c\delta^\beta\).
\item \textbf{(Contrast calibration.)} \(ab\le ch^\gamma\).
\item \textbf{(Occupancy.)} \(N\delta^d\le c_0\).
\end{itemize}

For the prescribed construction \(\mathfrak C\) of \cref{obj:def:marked-handle}, the weights on the finite sign arrays satisfy, for each hypothesis \(\theta\in\{-1,+1\}\),
\[
w_\theta(\lambda,\eta)\ge0
\quad\text{for every }\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I},
\qquad
\sum_{\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I}}
w_\theta(\lambda,\eta)=1.
\]
Every constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal M\), and its canonical contrast agrees everywhere on the unit cube with the deterministic contrast of its hypothesis:
\[
P_{\theta,\lambda,\eta}\in\mathcal M,
\qquad
\tau_{P_{\theta,\lambda,\eta}}(x)=\tau_\theta(x)
\quad
\bigl(x\in[0,1]^d\bigr).
\]
Thus the finite priors \(\varpi_\theta\) of the construction are supported on \(\mathcal M\).

The designated propensity function \(e_P\), restricted to the unit cube, has the same distribution under \(\varpi_{+1}\) and \(\varpi_{-1}\). At the interior evaluation profile
\[
x_0=(1/2,\ldots,1/2),
\]
the contrasts satisfy
\[
\tau_\theta(x_0)=-2\theta ab,
\qquad
\tau_{-1}(x_0)-\tau_{+1}(x_0)=4ab,
\qquad
cab\le4ab.
\]

Let \(M_{+1}\) and \(M_{-1}\) be the fixed-size mixture laws of the original-record experiment, with \(n\) labeled records and \(m\) auxiliary covariate-treatment records, under the respective priors. With the unhalved squared Hellinger distance of \cref{obj:def:hellinger},
\[
H^2(M_{+1},M_{-1})
\le CnNh^d\delta^da^2b^2.
\]

For every integer \(k_{\mathrm{aux}}\ge0\), the auxiliary mixture laws agree:
\[
\int P_{XA}^{\otimes k_{\mathrm{aux}}}\,d\varpi_{+1}(P)
=
\int P_{XA}^{\otimes k_{\mathrm{aux}}}\,d\varpi_{-1}(P).
\]
Their explicit conditional mixture kernels also agree for every collection of \(k_{\mathrm{aux}}\) covariates in \([0,1]^d\). For each hypothesis and every covariate \(x\in[0,1]^d\), the singleton labeled mixture has conditional law uniform on \(\{0,1\}^2\) for the treatment and observed response.

For every collection of \(N\) covariates in \([0,1]^d\), form the graph with vertices given by the records whose covariates lie in the localization cube \(C_h\) of \cref{obj:synth_3}, and edges between distinct vertices whose maximum-norm covariate distance is at most \(2\delta\). Conditional on these covariates, the mixed density factors as the product of the component densities over the connected components of this graph, for every hypothesis and every assignment of record spins. Every auxiliary-only component and every singleton labeled component has identical component densities under both hypotheses for every assignment of record spins, and hence the same full conditional law.

2eb2a1895098ae87200fc1f2a55853735e5e1d90.title: Constructed arm-mean functions
2eb2a1895098ae87200fc1f2a55853735e5e1d90.body:
The constructed real-valued arm-mean functions, with response perturbation amplitude \(b\), are defined for every dimension \(d\in\mathbb N\), parameters \(h,\delta,a,b\in\mathbb R\), hypothesis sign \(\theta\in\{-1,+1\}\), and response sign array \(\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I}\) by
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_{0,\theta,\eta}(x)
&=\frac12+b\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}
  \eta_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}(x)
  +\theta ab\,B_h(x)^2,\\
\mu_{1,\theta,\eta}(x)
&=\frac12+b\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}
  \eta_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}(x)
  -\theta ab\,B_h(x)^2,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\mathcal I\) is the finite frame index set at dimension \(d\) and scales \(h,\delta\) defined in \(\cref{obj:def:marked-handle}\). The localization bump \(B_h\) and localized frame entries \(\phi_{\mathbf z}\) are given by the defining formulas in \(\cref{obj:def:marked-handle}\), extended by those same formulas to every \(h,\delta\in\mathbb R\) and every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). The hypothesis sign and response signs encode Boolean values by assigning \(+1\) to true and \(-1\) to false. Each response sign is the encoded second component of the corresponding Boolean sign pair; the first component is arbitrary. Control and treatment correspond to false and true arm values, respectively.
